citeAs: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911.
creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (Google, Yale University)
description: IFEval is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark for large language models focused on "verifiable instructions" — instructions whose compliance can be objectively and automatically verified (e.g., "write in more than 400 words", "mention the keyword AI at least 3 times"). It consists of 25 types of verifiable instructions and around 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions, enabling fully automatic assessment of instruction-following ability.
name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Prompts were manually checked and edited one by one after automated generation and rephrasing steps. Verification of instruction-following is performed programmatically using deterministic functions (isfollowed) that check whether a model response satisfies each verifiable instruction, with both strict and loose accuracy metrics.
rai:dataCollection: Prompts were created through a four-step process: (1) generating base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended; (2) using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts; (3) applying another few-shot prompting approach to rephrase each prompt to increase phrasing diversity; and (4) manually checking and editing each rephrased prompt one by one.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts were generated by concatenating a base prompt (e.g., "write an essay") with multiple verifiable instructions. These were then filtered and rephrased using few-shot prompting before manual curation.
rai:dataLimitations: The current implementation can be improved by: (1) increasing the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions; (2) extending to multi-modal use cases. Additionally, very few instructions are 100% objectively and automatically verifiable — edge cases exist where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed (e.g., markdown formatting variations causing false negatives). The loose accuracy metric introduced to address false negatives may in turn introduce false positives.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each verifiable instruction has multiple variants in terms of parameters (e.g., "write 450 to 500 words" vs. "write 350 to 400 words") and phrasing (e.g., "write 450 to 500 words" vs. "your response must contain 450 to 500 words"), increasing diversity of the prompt set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Few-shot prompting was used to identify and remove illogical prompts (e.g., conflicting instructions). A second few-shot prompting pass rephrased prompts to increase diversity. Finally, all prompts were manually reviewed and edited.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to improve the safety and reliability of LLM implementations by providing objective, reproducible evaluation of instruction-following. The paper notes that discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs with potentially dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models using verifiable instructions; benchmarking LLMs on specific instruction types; identifying which types of instructions LLMs fail to follow; comparing different LLMs across various instruction categories.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Few-shot prompting with large language models was used to (1) identify and remove illogical prompts and (2) rephrase prompts to increase diversity during dataset construction.
